title: Using Euler's formula
description: convert between $e^{j\theta}$ and $\cos(\theta)+j\sin(\theta)$ as equivalent representations.

title: Identifying real and imaginary parts of a complex exponential
description: read the cosine term as the real part and the sine term as the imaginary part of $Ae^{j(\omega t+\phi)}$.

title: Interpreting polar form of a complex number
description: read $Ae^{j\phi}$ as a magnitude-angle representation of a complex quantity.

title: Converting complex numbers between rectangular and polar form
description: rewrite $a+jb$ as $|V|e^{j\angle V}$ by computing magnitude and angle.

title: Adding complex numbers in rectangular form
description: combine phasors by summing their real parts and imaginary parts separately.

title: Using special-angle values in the complex plane
description: recognize values like $e^{j\pi/2}=j$ and standard reference angles in phasor work.

title: Writing a cosine as a complex exponential
description: express $A\cos(\omega t+\phi)$ as the real part of $Ae^{j(\omega t+\phi)}$.

title: Factoring a sinusoid into phasor form
description: separate $Ae^{j(\omega t+\phi)}$ into a fixed phasor $Ae^{j\phi}$ and a rotating factor $e^{j\omega t}$.

title: Defining and interpreting a phasor
description: treat $V=Ae^{j\phi}$ as a stationary complex quantity that carries amplitude and phase.

title: Linking frequency sign to rotation direction
description: determine whether a complex exponential rotates clockwise or counterclockwise from the sign of $\omega$.

title: Rewriting sine and cosine with exponentials
description: use Euler identities to convert sine and cosine into sums or differences of exponentials.

title: Interpreting cosine as frequency components
description: recognize a real cosine as two counter-rotating exponentials with frequencies $+\omega$ and $-\omega$.

title: Interpreting frequency sign geometrically
description: understand positive and negative frequency as opposite directions of rotation in the complex plane.

title: Adding same-frequency cosines with phasors
description: convert each cosine to a phasor, add the phasors, and retain the common $e^{j\omega t}$ factor.

title: Forming the resultant phasor
description: combine same-frequency terms into one equivalent phasor with net amplitude and phase.

title: Converting a resultant phasor to a cosine
description: rewrite the summed phasor in polar form as a single cosine in amplitude-phase form.

title: Solving a full phasor addition problem
description: carry out phasor conversion, complex-domain addition, and conversion back to one real sinusoid.
